QuestionStmt.S: The value of $$\int_{0}^{2} [x^2] \, dx$$ is (where $[x]$ denotes the greatest integer function not greater than $x$)

Solution.S:
$$\int_{0}^{2} [x^2] \, dx = \int_{0}^{1} 0 \, dx + \int_{1}^{\sqrt{2}} 1 \, dx + \int_{\sqrt{2}}^{\sqrt{3}} 2 \, dx + \int_{\sqrt{3}}^{2} 3 \, dx$$

$$= 0 + 1(\sqrt{2} - 1) + 2(\sqrt{3} - \sqrt{2}) + 3(2 - \sqrt{3})$$

$$= \sqrt{2} - 1 + 2\sqrt{3} - 2\sqrt{2} + 6 - 3\sqrt{3}$$

$$= 5 - \sqrt{2} - \sqrt{3}$$

Final Answer: $$\boxed{5 - \sqrt{2} - \sqrt{3}}$$

Hence, the correct option is A.
